articles.title: Does personality predict family size? A 15,000-person study across three countries weighs in
articles.summary: A survey of 15,120 adults in Canada, the United States, and Japan suggests that outgoing, cooperative, and emotionally stable people tend to have slightly more biological children, though marriage, age, and national culture play much larger roles.

articles.title: A 30-minute walk helps sustain brain activity during mental task switching, study finds
articles.summary: Can a short walk change how your brain handles a mental challenge? In a small study, walking altered brain activity during a task-switching test, with some effects differing by age, though performance did not improve.

articles.title: Scientists finally pin down what a mysterious Alzheimer’s gene does
articles.summary: CASS4 has been tied to Alzheimer’s risk since 2013, but nobody knew what it did in the brain. New mouse research suggests it lets immune cells physically grip and compact amyloid plaques.

articles.title: Childhood trauma and ADHD independently fuel risky driving habits, study suggests
articles.summary: Driving can be dangerous for young adults with ADHD or a history of childhood trauma. New research explores how these two risk factors operate independently to increase the likelihood of speeding, texting, and aggressive behavior behind the wheel.

articles.title: New psychology study suggests your sexual turn-ons are far more fluid than assumed
articles.summary: Do sexual preferences stay fixed across adulthood? New research indicates that many adults experience moderate shifts in their sexual turn-ons over time, with no link to anxiety, depression, or sexual difficulties.

articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored for knowledge-intensive and safety-critical applications in nuclear engineering. articles.title: Chain-of-Thought Controllability Can Reduce Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is a promising tool for detecting hidden goals, off-task behavior, and other failures in AI agents. articles.title: How Much of SAR Vehicle Recognition Is the Vehicle? Background Shortcuts, Angle Gaps and Partial Libraries on MSTAR and ATRNet-STAR
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21827v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep networks score near 99% on the MSTAR vehicle benchmark, and the newer ATRNet-STAR benchmark was built to be harder. We ask how much of these scores comes from the vehicle itself. With a modern network (ConvNeXt-Small, 3 seeds) we first reproduce the known MSTAR result: with the central 96x96 pixels zeroed out, accuracy is still 73.3% (chance 10%). articles.title: Auditors Struggle to Catch Sabotage In End-to-End Transcripts of AI Safety Research
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As AI systems are increasingly used to automate AI R&D, misaligned systems could sabotage research intended to improve model safety and alignment. To stress-test defenses against such sabotage, we use a human expert as a proxy saboteur on AI safety research. We conduct a red-team/blue-team game where a human researcher runs AI safety experiments from scratch and auditors try to tell which were sabotaged and how. articles.title: DeltaHarness: Self-Evolving Harnesses for Resource-Adaptive Tool Execution
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21688v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using agents rely on execution harnesses to organize and schedule tool operations. The same task and resource description can conceal runtime conditions that reverse the latency ordering of valid execution plans. Resolving this uncertainty requires firsthand execution in the target setting. We introduce DeltaHarness, an execution-guided policy-search method that adapts agent harnesses from cold-start measurements. articles.title: The shape of individual differences in judgment: shared axes, personal weights, and when their spread crosses the consensus
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.22440v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: People differ in how they judge faces, artworks, photographs and jokes. Previous work measured the size of these differences; we ask what shape they take. We wrote three candidate shapes as nested generative models (same-sign reweighting of shared dimensions, a linear transform that allows reversal, and stimulus-specific offsets) and compared how well they predict people unseen in training, using ten public datasets (about 20,000 raters). articles.summary: arXiv:2611.22639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Central pattern generators (CPGs) provide a biologically inspired foundation for adaptive locomotor control, yet systematically characterizing their dynamic regimes in spiking neural networks remains challenging. articles.title: Tiny magnets deep inside the brain could transform Parkinson’s treatment
articles.summary: Scientists have developed a new technique that uses magnetic nanoparticles to stimulate deep brain regions, dramatically improving Parkinson’s-like movement problems in mice without permanently implanted electrodes. The breakthrough could pave the way for less invasive treatments using injectable particles and wearable magnetic headbands.
